desc: Build a brute-force BFS solver for small N to obtain exact answers.
Test the supplied run-length “good boundary” DP against brute force; confirm it fails on chains such as 1 2 1 3 2 3.
Explore the greedy pending-stack / max-of-two candidates and record counterexamples.
Implement a brute-force validator for the leader-by-last assignment model.
Implement the candidate O(M log N) run-level greedy solver and combine it with a safe upper-bound heuristic.
Run the leader-by-last validator against BFS on exhaustive/random small cases and report mismatches or optimal leader patterns.
If mismatches appear, inspect their optimal leader assignments to identify the missing structural constraint.
If no mismatches appear, derive a formal exchange proof for the run-level greedy rule and finalize it as the solution.
Determine how runs of length greater than 1 are handled in the validated model (element-level vs run-level) using BFS counterexamples.
Implement the final solution, validate on samples and brute-force cases, and handle large T efficiently.
